denigrate

DEN-ih-grayt · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To denigrate is to unfairly criticize or attack someone's character or reputation.

During the campaign, one candidate repeatedly denigrated her opponent's charity work, hinting it was nothing but a publicity stunt.

Worked Example

A jealous coworker quietly denigrated her colleague's promotion, telling anyone who would listen that it had nothing to do with talent.

The coworker wasn't offering fair criticism -- she was maliciously attacking a colleague's reputation out of jealousy, exactly what denigrate describes.

Your Turn

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

malign: To malign someone is to say harmful things about them that are often untrue -- the lie is part of the attack. Denigrate does not need falsehood: it unfairly runs down a person's character or work, often through sneering, belittling talk that twists true facts.

vilify: To vilify someone is to speak or write about them in abusively critical terms, painting them as a villain outright. Denigrate is quieter and more corrosive -- a drip of unfair, dismissive attacks on someone's character rather than one storm of open abuse.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

extol: to praise someone or something enthusiastically

laud: to praise highly

Where it sits · how far past fair the words go — criticize → denigrate → slander

criticize vs. denigrate: To criticize someone is simply to point out faults, which can be fair -- milder and more neutral than denigrate.

slander vs. denigrate: To slander someone is to make damaging false statements about them, especially in a way that could be legally actionable -- an even sharper attack than denigrate.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — de-

Prefix — de-: thoroughly (an intensifying use) (Latin)

Root — nigr-

Root — nigr-: black; to blacken (from Latin niger, 'black,' and nigrare, 'to blacken')

Suffix — -ate

Suffix — -ate: to make or do (Latin verb ending)

Put it together

Put it together: Denigrate combines de- ('thoroughly') + nigr- (from Latin niger, 'black,' nigrare 'to blacken') + -ate (verb ending) -- literally 'to blacken thoroughly.' To denigrate someone is to figuratively blacken their name or reputation.

Use the root in a new word: nigrescent

Use the root in a new word: nigrescent: Scientists sometimes describe cooling volcanic rock as nigrescent, meaning it is darkening or turning black.

Root Check

Word Choice

Denigrate describes an unfair, often repeated attack on someone's character or reputation -- notice how it's more personal than decry (which condemns actions or policies) and more malicious than deride (which mocks with open scorn).
